newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end modestly lower.

text.p: March 19 - U.S. debt futures ended modestly lower. Traders said June T-bonds slipped late to seven pct cash yield level, near 108-07/32 or so. But one dealer bought some 4,000 June futures in what some brokers called a hedge after they had rolled out of March futures that expired at noontime. They wait for Fed Greenspan's Congressional testimony Thursday. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/))E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
A German-owned bank also was seen buying the lows, another broker said.

Some traders expected range-trading to persist at least into Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Congressional testimony Thursday about monetary policy, interest rates and other issues starting at 0900 CST/1500 GMT.
Also Thursday, Fed governor Susan Phillips testifies to a Senate subcommittee on regulatory modifications.
But the second broker looked for nearby futures to resume their downward slant before next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and crack below the seven percent area.

"They may see a directional trade (down) for seven percent, and we actually had a seven-percent test today. Cash got there, and our equivalent crept up a bit," he said. "Will 108-07/32 hold us in? It's feeling a little bit shaky. There's not a whole lot of foundation here."
He also noted that April T-bond futures-options expire Friday at midday, which might give June futures another reason to gravitate down to the 108 strike.
The first broker agreed and looked for cash yield to probe the 7.04-05 percent level, which would equate a drop in June futures toward the 107-24/32 level.

Futures eroded early after February consumer price index showed very slightly more strength than expected. CPI rose 0.3 percent overall and gained 0.2 percent excluding food and energy. Economists on average had expected CPI to rise 0.2 percent overall and in the core rate.
They showed no response to Greenspan's comments Wednesday concerning banking supervision and regulation.

June T-bond ended down 6/32 at 108-15/32, T-notes eased 3/32 to 106-17/32, muni-bonds lost 2/32 to 113-00, Sept T-bills lost 0.030 bps to 94.430, and Eurodollars dipped 0.030 bps to 93.870. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
